summary: Focused regression of the iteration_126 follow-ups. BACKEND 24/25 pass: GAP 1 (update_lecture force) FIXED: warning -> 409 without force or with force=false, no DB change; force=true -> 200; 'force' key is not stored in the doc. Hard errors stay 400 even with force=true: same course, different course with the same teacher, room booked by a different teacher. Group change to a group whose teacher is busy -> 400 even with force. Group change with a students conflict -> 409, then force -> 200 and teacher_id is set to the group teacher. Non-scheduling fields (lesson_title set and clear, notes, time_locked true/false, status cancelled+reason+reason_type, back to scheduled) all return 200 without force on a lecture that already overlaps, so they are not conflict-checked. GAP 2 (reschedule teacher_override) FIXED: a group-1 lecture of HADRAMOUT rescheduled onto the slot of teacher 698ad3da's '180156' lecture -> 400 with and without force; a group-2 lecture to the same slot -> 200. All 13 original P0 reschedule/create tests from test_reschedule_conflict_force.py still pass. One NEW same-class gap found: in update_lecture (PUT /api/lectures/{id}), when an existing group lecture's date or time is changed WITHOUT 'group' in the body, the group teacher is not used (_eff_group_teacher stays None), so the clash is checked against the course's main teacher and the double-booking is accepted (200, lecture moved). FRONTEND: group-change modal tested end to end (it was never tested before). Choosing group 2 -> PUT {group:'2', force:false} -> 409 -> window.confirm shows the students warning with 'هل تريد المتابعة؟' exactly once. Cancel sends no extra request, the modal stays open and nothing changes. Accept -> PUT {force:true} 200, success toast 'تم تغيير مجموعة المحاضرة', modal closes, DB group=2 and teacher=698bc059. Reschedule modal: 409 -> confirm text has 'هل تريد المتابعة؟' once -> force retry 200 -> toast 'تم إعادة جدولة المحاضرة إلى 2026-11-03'.

critical.issue: Same bug class, last remaining path. _eff_group_teacher is only set inside `if 'group' in update_data`. For an EXISTING group lecture (lecture.group='1', whose group has its own teacher) a PUT with only {date/start_time/end_time/room} passes teacher_override=None, so check_teacher_lecture_conflict uses the course's main teacher. Reproduced: a '180156' lecture (teacher 698ad3da) on 2027-07-21 08:00 and a HADRAMOUT group-1 lecture (group teacher 698ad3da) on 2027-07-22. PUT {date:'2027-07-21'} -> 200 and the lecture moved; expected 400. Fix: initialise `_eff_group_teacher = lecture.get('teacher_id') if lecture.get('group') else None` before the `if 'group' in update_data` block, mirroring reschedule.

minor.issue: Still open from iteration_126: merge-group siblings that move together are not conflict-checked in the new slot.
Still returns 409, so the frontend shows a force confirm dialog for a non-bypassable DB-unique rejection (not re-tested, the code is unchanged).

issues: It still appends '\n\nهل تريد المتابعة؟' unconditionally. The room warning message itself does not include it, but the /room endpoint's students-conflict warning does, so that path would show the question twice. Apply the same msg.includes('المتابعة') guard.

action_items: update_lecture: default _eff_group_teacher to lecture.get('teacher_id') when the lecture already has a group and 'group' is not in the payload, so date/time/room edits of group lectures check the group teacher's clashes. Then run tests/test_update_lecture_conflict_force.py::TestUpdateGroupChange::test_group_lecture_date_change_uses_group_teacher.
Optional: add the msg.includes('المتابعة') de-dup guard to handleChangeRoom.
Optional (carried over): conflict-check apply_to_shared siblings, and use a non-409 code for DuplicateKeyError.
critical_code_review_comments: update_lecture now mirrors reschedule correctly: error -> 400 unconditionally; warning -> 409 unless force (teacher + room); students check added; 'force' is excluded from update_data.

reschedule_lecture: teacher_override=lecture.teacher_id for group lectures. If a group has no own teacher, lecture.teacher_id is the main teacher (or None -> falls back to the course teacher). Correct.

Root cause of the remaining gap is the same drift: the 'effective teacher' is derived differently in each endpoint. A shared helper resolve_effective_group_teacher(lecture, new_group) plus one enforce_conflicts(...) would close this class for good. server.py is 19.5k lines.

success_rate.backend: 24/25 (96%). The only failure is the new update_lecture group-teacher gap.

rca of the issue: Remaining gap: in update_lecture the group teacher is resolved only when the payload changes 'group'. Repro: T180156 lecture on D at 08:00; HADRAMOUT group-1 lecture on D+1; PUT /api/lectures/{g1} {date:D} -> 200 (should be 400). Mitigation: initialise _eff_group_teacher from the existing lecture's group or teacher_id before the group-change block.
